app.tagline: The Bulgarian Volunteer Corps in the War of Liberation

ch.ploesti.title: The Camp at Ploiești
ch.ploesti.intro: Near Ploiești in Romania the camp of the Bulgarian Volunteer Corps is established — a volunteer formation within the Russian Danube Army. Initially 6 companies of around 7,400 men are formed; later the corps grows to 12 companies and nearly 10,000 men. Command is entrusted to General Nikolay Stoletov. Train and equip the companies for the march south.
ch.ploesti.fact1: At first the Russian command assigned the volunteers auxiliary — convoy and supply — duties, but their training and enthusiasm quickly turned them into a real combat force.
ch.ploesti.fact2: The corps was attached to the Advance Detachment of Lieutenant-General Iosif Gurko.
ch.ploesti.mechanic.hint: Tap each company to train and equip it.
ch.ploesti.mechanic.done: The six companies are ready to march!
ch.samara_flag.title: The Samara Flag
ch.samara_flag.intro: The symbol of the corps becomes the Samara Flag — a tricolour made by nuns in the Russian city of Samara and given to the Bulgarian volunteers. The solemn presentation to the Third Volunteer Company takes place at Ploiești. Before the flag the volunteers swear an oath of loyalty. Arrange the flag and raise it before the ranks.
ch.samara_flag.fact1: The Samara Flag is the only flag in Bulgarian history later decorated with the Order of Bravery.
ch.samara_flag.fact2: After the war the flag was kept in Radomir, hometown of its last bearer Nikola Korchev.
ch.samara_flag.mechanic.hint: Drag the tricolour into the right order: red, white, green.
ch.samara_flag.mechanic.oath: The oath is sworn. The flag is sacred!
ch.danube.title: The Danube at Svishtov
ch.danube.intro: The Russian army successfully crosses the Danube at Svishtov and secures a bridgehead south of the river. The army splits into three detachments; the smallest — the Advance Detachment of about 12,500 men — includes the volunteer companies. Ferry the boats across the river, launching them in the calm moments between enemy volleys.
ch.danube.fact1: The Advance Detachment pushed rapidly south through Tarnovo toward the Balkan passes, outrunning the enemy.
ch.danube.fact2: Crossing the Danube opened the road into Thrace.
ch.danube.mechanic.hint: Tap when the marker is in the green zone to send a boat across.
ch.stara_zagora.title: Stara Zagora
ch.stara_zagora.intro: At Stara Zagora the Bulgarian Volunteer Corps receives its baptism of fire against the vast army of Suleiman Pasha. The Third Company under Lieutenant-Colonel Pavel Kalitin takes the main blow and fights a desperate battle to save the Samara Flag. Lead the flag-bearer out of the encirclement — do not let the enemy reach him.
ch.stara_zagora.fact1: In a single day five bearers and commander Kalitin himself fell around the flag; the sacred banner was carried off the field after fierce hand-to-hand fighting.
ch.stara_zagora.fact2: The battle was lost tactically, but morally it was a victory — the corps proved its worth and saved its flag.
ch.stara_zagora.mechanic.hint: Drag to guide the flag-bearer. Avoid the enemy soldiers!
ch.shipka.title: Shipka
ch.shipka.intro: Suleiman Pasha's army — about 27,000 regulars — storms the Shipka Pass, the key to Northern Bulgaria. Short of troops, Gen. Stoletov holds only the peaks. When ammunition runs out, the defenders repel the assaults with stones, logs and bayonets. Hold the position until Gen. Radetzky's reinforcements arrive!
ch.shipka.fact1: Over the three hardest days the Shipka detachment lost about 3,100 Russian soldiers and 535 Bulgarian volunteers; Turkish losses exceeded 8,200.
ch.shipka.fact2: Suleiman Pasha's army failed to cross the pass and relieve Pleven — the turning point of the war.
ch.shipka.fact3: Ivan Vazov dedicated his ode "The Volunteers at Shipka" to the heroic defence.
ch.shipka.mechanic.hint: Tap enemies to fire. When ammo runs out — throw stones!
ch.pleven_march.title: Pleven and the Winter March
ch.pleven_march.intro: After the capitulation of Osman Pasha's army at Pleven, large Russian forces are freed for a general offensive across the Balkan Mountains. In harsh winter conditions Gen. Gurko's detachment crosses the western passes and on 23 December / 4 January liberates Sofia. Choose the column's route across the snowbound Balkan.
ch.pleven_march.fact1: The Bulgarian Volunteer Corps took part in the winter offensive within the Russian detachments.
ch.pleven_march.fact2: On 23 December 1877 / 4 January 1878 Gurko's detachment liberated Sofia.
ch.pleven_march.mechanic.hint: Choose a path at each fork to lead the column across the Balkan.
ch.pleven_march.mechanic.choiceFast: The direct path over the ridge
ch.pleven_march.mechanic.arrived: The column reached the sub-Balkan plain!
ch.sheynovo.title: Shipka–Sheynovo
ch.sheynovo.intro: The final great battle of the Southern front is fought at Sheynovo, in cold of about minus 20 degrees. Gen. Radetzky splits his forces into three columns — Svyatopolk-Mirsky's, Skobelev's, and the central one under Radetzky himself. Lead the three columns in a coordinated attack on the fortified Turkish camp.
ch.sheynovo.fact1: Vessel Pasha's army capitulated; between 22,000 and 23,000 men were captured along with three pashas.
ch.sheynovo.fact2: The Balkan defensive line was broken and the road to Edirne and Constantinople lay open.
ch.sheynovo.mechanic.hint: Launch each column when its indicator is green. All three must strike together!
ch.sheynovo.mechanic.won: The camp is crushed! Vessel Pasha capitulates!
ch.liberation.title: The Liberation
ch.liberation.intro: After the rout at Sheynovo the Russian advance toward Constantinople is unstoppable. The war ends with the signing of the Preliminary Treaty of San Stefano. The Third of March becomes the symbol of the Liberation and is today Bulgaria's national holiday.
ch.liberation.fact1: By Order No. 13 of 15 July 1878 the 12 volunteer companies became infantry battalions of the Bulgarian Land Army — the nucleus of the future Bulgarian army.
ch.liberation.fact2: The deeds at Stara Zagora and Shipka remain central symbols of national memory, immortalized by Vazov and in the monuments at Shipka and Stara Zagora.
ch.liberation.mechanic.epilogue1: The Bulgarian Volunteer Corps is the brightest military expression of the national liberation movement.
ch.liberation.mechanic.epilogue2: From the camp at Ploiești, through the baptism of fire at Stara Zagora and the epic of Shipka, to the rout at Sheynovo — the volunteers defended the Samara Flag with their lives.

credits.history.text: The Bulgarian Volunteer Corps, the Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878), and the battles of Stara Zagora, Shipka and Sheynovo — based on open historical sources.
